notes: Fixtures are generated by make_fixtures.py. Every eval runs against a generated fixture repository — nothing here depends on a private codebase.

docx_produced.text: Produced a .docx file, not only Markdown or plain text

md_mirror.text: Produced a Markdown mirror of comparable substance beside the .docx

figure_embedded.text: At least one generated diagram is embedded in the document

rebuildable.text: Saved the build/render scripts, so the document can be regenerated

cover_and_contents.text: Has a cover with metadata and a contents section

findings_section.text: Includes a findings, open-questions or notable-observations section

evals.name: schema-doc-backend
evals.objective: Produce a schema reference that explains what constraints mean, not just that they exist.

repo.characteristics: FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + Alembic. Three tables. CHECK constraints encoding real business rules (facility limit, positive principal, approval attribution). Cascades differ per relationship: RESTRICT on loans->borrowers, CASCADE on repayments->loans. Migration 0002 names a constraint differently from the model.

evals.prompt: Write a database schema reference for this service. The constraints encode business rules that aren't documented anywhere and people keep getting them wrong.
evals.expected_output: A .docx plus .md mirror with column-level tables, each constraint explained in terms of the rule it enforces, cascade behaviour documented per relationship, an ER-style figure, and the model/migration constraint-name divergence flagged.

assertions.text: Covers all three tables
Uses column-level tables including nullability
Explains the facility-limit and approval-attribution constraints as business rules
Documents the differing cascade behaviour (RESTRICT vs CASCADE)
Flags that the model and migration name the facility constraint differently
Cites the model files repeatedly

evals.name: api-contracts-backend
evals.objective: Document endpoints with request, response and error shapes, grouped usefully.

repo.characteristics: Two routers, eight endpoints, a lifecycle with VALID_TRANSITIONS in the service layer.

evals.prompt: We're onboarding a partner team that needs to integrate with this API. Can you write up the API contracts for them?
evals.expected_output: A .docx plus .md mirror listing every endpoint with method, path, purpose and error cases; the loan lifecycle transitions explained; an endpoint-map figure; source citations.

assertions.text: Covers all eight endpoints
States HTTP methods
Explains the loan status transitions rather than only listing routes
Documents error or failure responses

evals.name: architecture-backend
evals.objective: Explain the shape and the reasoning, not the directory listing.

repo.characteristics: Clear api/services/models layering with a ledger call outside the transaction in disburse().

evals.prompt: New engineer joins next week. Write them an architecture overview of this service.
evals.expected_output: A .docx plus .md mirror describing purpose, layering, request flow, data at rest, and notable risks — including the ledger call sitting outside the disbursement transaction.

assertions.text: Describes the api / services / models layering
Notes that the ledger post sits outside the transaction
Explains reasoning rather than only enumerating directories

evals.name: sequence-flow-doc
evals.objective: Document a multi-step flow with its transaction boundary and failure modes.

repo.characteristics: Checkout: reserve stock (external, pre-transaction), commit order, charge AFTER commit, then non-transactional side effects. Payment client is explicitly non-idempotent. Inventory client has no timeout.

evals.prompt: The checkout flow keeps causing incidents and nobody can agree on what actually happens in what order. Document it properly.
evals.expected_output: A .docx plus .md mirror with a sequence figure marking the transaction boundary, each step named, and the failure modes called out — committed order with no payment, non-idempotent retry, missing timeout.

assertions.text: Names the four stages of the flow
Identifies what is inside the transaction and what is not
Flags the committed-order-without-payment window
Flags the non-idempotent charge
Produced at least one figure for the flow

evals.name: frontend-only-doc
evals.objective: Document a repo with no backend, without inventing one.

repo.characteristics: React + TS + Vite. Routes, zustand store, axios client with request interceptor and no refresh handling. No server code anywhere.

evals.prompt: document this frontend repo for a new starter
evals.expected_output: A .docx plus .md mirror covering routing, state, the API client and the auth token handling; no database or backend sections invented; the missing token-refresh path noted.

assertions.text: Identifies React, TypeScript and Vite
Covers routing, state management and the API layer
Does not claim the repository has a database or server-side persistence
Notes the token handling, including the absent refresh path
Cites frontend source paths

evals.name: no-database-honesty
evals.objective: EDGE CASE. Must not fabricate a schema section for a service with no persistence.

repo.characteristics: Stateless FastAPI conversion service. In-memory TTL cache only. README states there is no database.

evals.prompt: Generate the documentation set for this service — architecture, schema, API, whatever applies.
evals.expected_output: Architecture and API documentation. Either no schema document at all, or an explicit statement that the service has no persistent storage. Any invented tables are a hard failure.

assertions.text: HARD FAIL — does not invent tables, columns or DDL

check.comment: Only patterns that cannot appear in a truthful DENIAL. Words like 'migration' or 'primary key' are excluded: an honest document says 'there is no migration tool', and an absence check cannot read negation.

assertions.text: States explicitly that there is no persistent storage
Explains the in-memory cache and its TTL
Documents the upstream dependency and what happens when it fails

evals.name: minimal-api-proportionality
evals.objective: EDGE CASE. A two-endpoint service should get a short document, not a padded one.

repo.characteristics: One Flask file, two endpoints, no database, no services.

evals.prompt: can you document this little service
evals.expected_output: A short accurate document covering both endpoints. Padding to fill a template is the failure mode being tested.

assertions.text: Covers both endpoints
Stays proportionate — under ~18,000 characters of prose
Does not over-illustrate a three-file service (at most 3 figures)
Does not invent persistence

evals.name: monorepo-structure
evals.objective: EDGE CASE. Document a multi-package repo and the contract between packages.

repo.characteristics: packages/api (Express + Prisma), packages/web (React), packages/shared (types + canTransition). Both sides import the shared status model.

evals.prompt: we've got a monorepo here — api, web and a shared package. document how it all fits together for someone joining the team
evals.expected_output: A .docx plus .md mirror naming all three packages, explaining the shared-types contract and that changing it affects both sides, covering the Prisma schema and the status transition rules.

assertions.text: Names all three packages
Explains that the shared package is imported by both sides
Covers the shipment status model and transition rules
Documents the Prisma models

evals.name: incomplete-project-honesty
evals.objective: EDGE CASE. Must distinguish what works from what is a stub.

repo.characteristics: Employee/shift CRUD works. The solver raises NotImplementedError throughout and is called from nowhere. assign_shift raises. notifications is a pass-stub. README says most of it does not work.

evals.expected_output: Documentation that clearly separates working functionality from unimplemented stubs, and does not describe the solver or notifications as if they function.

assertions.text: States plainly that parts are unimplemented
Identifies the scheduling solver specifically as non-functional
Covers the employee and shift domain objects
assertions.comment: Deliberately does NOT assert that CRUD works. Runs correctly concluded that nothing in this fixture works — the README's 'Done: employee CRUD' claim is false, both bodies are '...'. An assertion demanding they be described as working would penalise the right answer.

assertions.text: HARD FAIL — does not describe the solver as operational

evals.name: mixed-stack-coverage
evals.objective: EDGE CASE. Cover three languages as one system, not three disconnected write-ups.

repo.characteristics: Python API enqueues to Redis, Node worker consumes and renders, Go CLI inspects and requeues. The worker has no retry and no dead-letter queue — failed jobs are lost.

evals.prompt: document tilepipe. it's python, node and go and I want one document that explains the whole thing rather than three.
evals.expected_output: A single document covering all three components, the Redis queue as the integration point, and the lost-job failure mode.

assertions.text: Covers all three components
Identifies Redis as the integration point between them
Flags that a failed render is lost with no retry or dead-letter queue
Produced a single coherent document rather than three

evals.name: auth-authorization-doc
evals.objective: Document the role model, the policy layer and the token handling — including a real vulnerability.

repo.characteristics: Five roles with a rank ladder; auditor sits outside it. Policy module with can_read/can_edit/can_approve/can_delete, including a no-self-approval rule. verify() does not check the `typ` claim, so a refresh token is accepted as an access token.

evals.prompt: write up how auth and permissions work in vaultdesk — who can do what, and how it's enforced
evals.expected_output: A .docx plus .md mirror with a role table, the rank ladder, a capability matrix, where enforcement happens, and the refresh-token-accepted-as-access-token flaw called out.

assertions.text: Covers all five roles
Explains the rank ladder and that auditor sits outside it
Identifies the policy module as the enforcement point
Documents the no-self-approval rule
Flags that the token type claim is unchecked, so a refresh token works as an access token
Presents a capability matrix or per-role permission table

evals.name: repo-analysis-detection
evals.objective: Detect the stack and propose the right document set before writing anything.

repo.characteristics: Express + Prisma + React across three packages.

evals.prompt: have a look at this repo and tell me what documentation it needs, then write the most useful one
evals.expected_output: An explicit proposal naming the detected stack and the document types worth writing, with a recommendation, followed by one document.

assertions.text: Names the detected stack correctly
Discusses which document types apply to this repository
Some analysis output or rationale is preserved with the deliverable

evals.name: full-set-backend
evals.objective: Produce a coherent multi-document set with consistent formatting and cross-references.

repo.characteristics: Supports architecture, schema and API documents.

evals.prompt: produce the full documentation set for this backend — architecture, schema and API contracts
evals.expected_output: Three .docx files plus mirrors, consistent cover and section conventions across all of them, and cross-references between them.

assertions.text: Produced three distinct documents
Covers architecture, schema and API subject matter
Documents reference one another
Produced several figures across the set

evals.name: update-existing-document
evals.objective: Edit the build script and rebuild, rather than hand-editing the .docx.

repo.characteristics: Run this after e01. The prior build scripts are in the workspace.

evals.prompt: the schema doc you produced needs a section on indexes and one on retention. add them and rebuild.
evals.expected_output: An updated .docx and .md with the two new sections, produced by editing and rerunning the build script — the script must show the new sections.

assertions.text: Both requested sections are present
The build script itself contains the new sections, proving it was regenerated not hand-edited
The original content survives the edit
